summary: Store plan step 2: App Store configuration for the Expo iOS app. app.json sets ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false and supportsTablet false; eas.json adds a store build profile (distribution store, remote build numbers, autoIncrement) and a store submit profile that reads the App Store Connect API key from environment variables; iOS dictation prefers on-device recognition when the recognizer supports it. These are native changes and need a new iOS build, not an OTA.

desktop.reason: Only apps/mobile config, apps/mobile/src/lib/voice.ts and docs change; the desktop app is untouched.

nativeAndroid.reason: The Play app is the native Kotlin app, which already uses the platform SpeechRecognizer (AndroidSpeechRecognizerGateway) with no on-device request; it ships through Play, so the App Store keys and EAS profiles do not apply. The Expo app's Android dictation is left on the default recognizer on purpose.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No wire protocol or backend change.

automated: npx expo config --type introspect shows ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false and supportsTablet false in the resolved iOS config.
The eas-json resolver loads the store build and submit profiles and substitutes the ASC_API_KEY_* variables.
npx expo-doctor stays at 20/21 (the one failure is the existing 15 out-of-date packages).
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.
notExercised: A store build on EAS and eas submit (needs a new iOS build and the App Store record; not run from this job).
On-device dictation on a physical iPhone, and the fallback on a locale without an on-device model.
